# Verify the finish gate names both engine SHAs on a lagging-pin build failure

Parent: **MS-0MVZZ767V009KG3F** — verification of **AC1** (and the AC3 constraint). Verification-only: no framework code is edited from this repo (repository boundary, Q1=A precedent on `MS-0MVSB1OVW00178W6`).

**Unblocked 2026-11-04** (re-checked read-only by the `plan` skill). The framework item `SA-0MW06FLFR009F0P4` — *Finish gate: report a lagging engine pin when the build fails after engine:sync* — is now **`completed` / `in_review`** with commit **`e2e2d24ca`** recorded on it, and that commit **is an ancestor of `origin/dev`** in SorraAgents. Unblock condition audit:

- `engine_lag` reporting exists: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` has 12 `engine_lag` matches on `origin/dev`, and the **installed runtime copy** `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` also has 12 (refreshed), so a `implement.py finish` run on this repo can now report the condition.
- The both-SHAs build-failure comment and the stdout tail are in `_build_failure_message()`; the structured field is `report["steps"]["build"]["engine_lag"]`.
- Expected shape (settled; cited from the "Engine lag on a failed build" section of `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`, per its field table): `engine_lag.advanced` (bool) and `engine_lag.submodules[]` with `submodule`, `pinned_sha`, `composed_sha`, `advanced`. Note the earlier unknown "whether the field name settles as `engine_lag`" is now **resolved: it settled as `engine_lag`**.
- Fixture coverage landed in `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_engine_lag.py` (6 tests); `skill/test_cache.py` (`compute_git_state`), `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs` and the pin policy are **not** in commit `e2e2d24ca`'s diff (`docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` + `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` + 2 test files only).
- The previous `blocked` status was already released to `open` by the last run; this re-check therefore only records the unblock evidence — no status change was needed.

**Cross-store dependency (prose only):** the MS worklog cannot hold a `wl dep` edge to an SA item, so this relationship is declared here and by convention, as with `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4`.

## Goal

As an implement agent, I need proof that when a lagging engine pin makes the build itself fail, the finish report and the build-failure comment name **both** the pinned SHA and the engine SHA the build compiled against — so I can tell an engine-induced build failure from a source failure instead of chasing a compile error the item never caused.

## Acceptance Criteria

### Parent ACs this child verifies (restated)

- [ ] The condition "pre-build pin lags the engine tracked tip and the build failed" is visible in the finish report and the build-failure comment, naming both SHAs.
- [ ] No cache-key or pin-policy change without producer sign-off.

### Verification detail

- [ ] Live proof on **this repo**: from a throwaway worktree created at a commit whose `configs/engine-pin.json` lags the engine tracked tip, a `implement.py finish` run whose build fails reports **both** the pinned SHA and the advanced engine SHA in (a) the finish report's build step — `report["steps"]["build"]["engine_lag"]`, i.e. `advanced: true` and a `submodules` entry whose `pinned_sha` and `composed_sha` are both non-null and different — and (b) the build-failure comment posted on the work item.
- [ ] The build-failure comment contains the `engine:sync: core updated <from> → <to>` line (i.e. the build's stdout is represented, not stderr alone).
- [ ] The reproduction is recorded with its facts: worktree base commit, pinned SHA, engine tip SHA, exit code, and sanitised log path — consistent with the recorded probe (`a6ef0b7d`, pinned `21bedf7a`, engine tip `2305f888`).
- [ ] **No false diagnosis:** a build failure with no engine advance (or a repo with no submodule) reports no engine-lag condition. Verified from the SorraAgents fixture tests, cited by path and test name: `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_engine_lag.py::test_failed_build_without_an_advance_reports_no_lag`, `::test_repo_without_submodules_reports_no_lag`, `::test_item_originated_composition_is_not_a_build_advance` and `::test_failed_advance_without_sync_output_is_handled`; the positive cases are `::test_failed_build_after_engine_advance_reports_the_lag` and `::test_failed_build_comment_reproduces_the_engine_sync_line`.
- [ ] **AC3 constraint — no cache-key or pin-policy change:** confirmed by reading the `SA-0MW06FLFR009F0P4` diff (commit hash recorded here) that `compute_git_state` (`skill/test_cache.py`) is untouched and `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs` is untouched; no verify-only / pinned-composition sync was introduced.
- [ ] Evidence recorded on this item: log paths, the finish-report JSON fragment, the comment id, and the SA commit hash. Any deviation is raised as a new work item, never worked around here.

## Constraints

- No `.pi/` or framework edits from this repo; no changes to `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs`.
- Runs go through the test skill / the finish gate, never ad-hoc suites.
- The probe worktree is reset and removed afterwards; nothing is pushed from it except this item's own evidence commit.
- If the report turns out to require a change of build composition (Option B) rather than additive reporting, stop and raise it for producer sign-off.

## Key Files

- `configs/engine-pin.json`, `.gitmodules`, `package.json` (`build` runs `engine:sync` first)
- `core/scripts/engine-sync.mjs` — canonical sync/verify behaviour under verification (read-only)
- `tests/tooling/engine-checkout-precheck.ts`, `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts` — existing lag guards to reuse when constructing the lagging-pin worktree
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — the published limitation note this verification keeps honest
- `docs/dev/analysis/ac1-finish-gate-composition-verification.md` — the recorded "Observations and limits" that this condition first appeared in
- SorraAgents (read-only): `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`_engine_lag`, `_build_failure_message`), `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_engine_lag.py` (the fixture tests cited under "No false diagnosis"), `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_gate_build_churn.py` (hermetic real-submodule harness), `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (the `engine_lag` field table)

## Evidence

- Failing build log: `/tmp/ms0mvtevk8-ac1-probe-build.log`; clean-run probe at `99489ad8`: `/tmp/ms0mvtevk8-ac1-probe.json`.
- Parent reproduction record: `MS-0MVTEVK8S0078QC4` and `docs/dev/analysis/ac1-finish-gate-composition-verification.md`.
- **Unblock evidence (2026-11-04, read-only):** SorraAgents `SA-0MW06FLFR009F0P4` `completed` / `in_review`; commit `e2e2d24ca` is an ancestor of `origin/dev`; `grep -c engine_lag` → 12 in both the SorraAgents checkout and the installed runtime copy.
- **Live lagging-pin state at planning time (2026-11-04):** this repo's `dev`/`origin/dev` HEAD is `dc42eae3`, which records gitlink `d46eb242` in `configs/engine-pin.json`; the engine tracked tip is `b3cf4877` — **6 commits ahead**. A fresh throwaway worktree at `dev` HEAD therefore starts lagging and `engine:sync` will advance it, which is exactly the condition AC1 needs. (The main checkout currently carries that advance as **staged** changes to `configs/engine-pin.json` and `core` — left behind by an earlier session, untouched by this planning run; the probe worktree must be created from `HEAD`, and the advance must not be committed as part of this item's evidence commit.)
- Note for the implementer: reproducing a **build failure** (not just an advance) needs source that predates a breaking engine API change — the recorded `hasChoices` → `isChoice` rename at `a6ef0b7d` is the known-good seed. If the lagging engine at `dev` HEAD no longer breaks the current source, use a throwaway checkout of the recorded base (`a6ef0b7d`, pin `21bedf7a`) as the reproduction subject and record the actual SHAs used.

# Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` in tce-main-street

## Why

This project's worklog database is behind the installed `wl` version. Every `wl` invocation prints:

```
Worklog: database at /home/rgardler/projects/tce-main-street/.worklog/worklog.db has schemaVersion=8 but the application expects schemaVersion=9. Required columns were repaired automatically. see 'wl doctor upgrade' to list and apply pending migrations
```

Required columns are being patched on every invocation instead of migrated, and the git hooks are stale. Discovered during the 2026-11-04 downtime-dispatcher RCA (the same finding exists across the other worklog roots).

## Pending work (from `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json`)

### Schema migrations (6)

- `20260210-add-needsProducerReview` — Add needsProducerReview INTEGER column to workitems (default 0)
- `20260315-add-audit` — Legacy: Add audit TEXT column to workitems (now replaced by audit_results table)
- `20260604-backfill-audit-results` — Backfill audit_results from existing workitems.audit JSON column
- `20260604-drop-audit-column` — Drop legacy audit TEXT column from workitems table (replaced by audit_results) **[UNSAFE]**
- `20260923-add-audit-fingerprint` — Add nullable fingerprint column to audit_results for content-based freshness gate (WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K)
- `20261015-drop-needsProducerReview` — Legacy: Drop needsProducerReview column (reverted — the flag was restored by 20261016-restore-needsProducerReview) **[UNSAFE]**

### Outdated git hooks

- pre-push, post-merge, post-rewrite

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want this project's worklog schema and git hooks fully up to date, so that `wl` stops auto-patching columns on every call and so every worklog hook behaves like the current template.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` afterwards reports `pending: []` and no hook whose `status` is not `up-to-date`.
2. `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` was executed against this project's database and applied the migrations listed above.
3. A plain `wl list --json` invocation no longer prints the `schemaVersion=8 … expects schemaVersion=9` warning.
4. **Data-safety check.** The count of items with `needsProducerReview == true` is identical before and after:
   `wl list --json | jq '[.workItems[] | select(.needsProducerReview == true)] | length'`
   Record both numbers on this item.
5. `wl doctor` reports no new findings attributable to this upgrade (any residual finding is recorded on a follow-up item, not ignored).
6. The before/after `--dry-run --json` output is recorded in a comment on this item.

## Plan

1. Capture the baseline: `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` plus the `needsProducerReview` count → comment on this item.
2. Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm`.
3. Re-run `--dry-run` (expect nothing pending) and re-check the `needsProducerReview` count (must be unchanged).
4. If the upgrade touched tracked files (`.githooks/`, hook templates), commit them following build → test → commit order.

## Risks & notes

- `--confirm` applies migrations **non-interactively, including UNSAFE ones**. Review the `[UNSAFE]` entries above before running. The database is the runtime source of truth (SQLite); never edit `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` and never run `wl import` (destructive).
- If the `needsProducerReview` count changes, STOP, restore, and raise a `bug` against ContextHub's `wl` migration set instead of continuing — the drop/re-add cycle is the suspected cause of the permanent schema-8 oscillation.

## Provenance

Created from the 2026-11-04 overnight zero-dispatch RCA. Pi session `herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004`, log `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-ContextHub--/2026-11-04T07-55-10-163Z_herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004.jsonl`.

**Unsafe migrations in this sweep:** `20260604-drop-audit-column`, `20261015-drop-needsProducerReview`
data.title: Run wl doctor upgrade --confirm: apply pending schema migrations and refresh outdated git hooks
